transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood Solutions Eng); Daniel (CTO), Maria (Head InfoSec), Samir (ML Eng), Renee (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Lyric's on-prem, air-gapped requirements for an LLM inference platform; focus on offline updates, hardware constraints, KMS/HSM integrations, and auditability.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time, I'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this opp. quick intros?
[00:06] Daniel: yeah Daniel Park, CTO at Lyric, thanks for taking this.
[00:09] Maria: Maria Lopez, head of information security.
[00:12] Samir: Samir Patel, ML engineering.
[00:14] Priya: Priya Shah, solutions engineer at Redwood. Jordan on the call as well.
[00:20] Alex: great, goal for today is to understand your constraints around air-gapped on-prem deployment, timelines, and success criteria. we'll also cover how we do offline updates and support.

[00:38] Daniel: high level, we need to host everything in our colos, no egress to the public cloud, so air-gapped is hard requirement. sensitive patient data from trials, so we got strict regs. we'll need KMS/HSM integration and full audit log retention for 7 years, ish.
[00:52] Maria: and SSO must be SAML with SCIM provisioning; we also do annual SOC2 and are looking at ISO27001 soon. can you survive those audit questions?
[01:05] Priya: yes on the auth side, Redwood Private has SAML/SCIM + RBAC, and we support integrating with customer KMS, including HSMs. we do generate detailed audit logs, but we should validate retention configs match your retention policy.
[01:20] Samir: a few infra notes - our current infra is a mix of A100 and some older V100s, on-prem. we want to know Redwood's supported hardware and best practices for quantized models; also offline model updates are a must because we can't pull from a public repo.
[01:36] Jordan: thanks Samir. to confirm, we support on-prem deployment packages that work in air-gapped environments; model artifacts and container images can be delivered via secure offline media. we also have a secure update process that customers run locally - it's basically an offline bundle + verification signatures.
[01:52] Maria: how do you handle signing and verification? we need cryptographic attestations and ability to rotate keys; we can't have private keys stored on vendor side.
[02:02] Priya: we use signed update artifacts. Redwood signs release bundles, but customers perform final verification using their own KMS/HSM-stored verification keys. that way the vendor can't push unverified code.
[02:16] Daniel: timeline wise, we're aiming for a pilot in Q3, production by Q4. license/budget cycles close mid-July. we'll need pricing for reserved/dedicated capacity vs private on-prem license.
[02:30] Alex: noted, we'll include both pricing models - monthly commit for dedicated vs one-time platform + support for private.

[02:45] Maria: auditability - we need immutable logs, tamper-evidence, and exportable artifacts for auditors. what's the access model for logs?
[02:54] Priya: logs are shipped to your local ELK/Splunk or S3-compatible object store in your VPC/on-prem. we also support WORM-style retention if you attach to compliant storage. logs include token-level metadata, request traces, and model versioning info.
[03:12] Renee: storage concerns - our object store is Ceph and we prefer to avoid vendor-managed dbs. is that supported?
[03:18] Jordan: yes Ceph and on-prem S3-compatible stores are supported, we can write to customer endpoints, no outbound required.
[03:25] Samir: what's the recommended GPU memory for typical LLMs? our main use cases are instruction-following chat and embeddings for search across clinical notes. sequence lengths usually 1k-2k tokens.
[03:38] Priya: for 1k-2k sequences, if you're planning to run a 13B dense model, 80GB A100 or H100 is ideal with tensor-slicing options. for cost-sensitive, we can recommend 4-bit quantized variants that drop memory but require specific kernel support. we'll send a sizing spreadsheet.
[03:57] Daniel: we have older V100s - do you support mixed clusters?
[04:02] Jordan: we do recommend homogeneous pools for predictability, but we can route requests based on model variants and hardware capability. Redwood's smart routing can fallback to CPU or smaller models if needed, but performance will change.
[04:16] Maria: encryption at rest - we need to use our KMS, not vendor keys. can we bring our own keys?
[04:22] Priya: yes, BYOK supported. integration patterns include KMIP, AWS KMS proxies for private cloud, and direct HSM attachment for signing/verification.
[04:34] Samir: offline updates - can you walk through the process? say we need to patch runtime + model weights.
[04:41] Priya: high-level: we generate an update bundle that includes container images, runtime patches, model artifacts, and a signed manifest. That bundle is handed to you securely (sftp or physical media). On your side, an update agent verifies signatures via your local HSM and then applies the update; rollout can be staged across pools. We support tagging and rollback.
[05:03] Maria: we require reproducible builds and supply-chain attestations - can Redwood provide SBOMs and signed provenance?
[05:10] Priya: yes, SBOMs and provenance metadata are included in the bundle; we can provide CI/CD pipeline attestations and vulnerability scan outputs.
[05:20] Samir: curious about latency - for our app, 95p latency target is sub-200ms for short prompts, and throughput around 50 rps. what's realistic on-prem?
[05:31] Jordan: sub-200ms is possible on H100/A100 with local network and model optimization (quantization, kernel selection). If you need that consistently at 50 rps, we recommend 2-4 GPUs in a dedicated pool with batching tuned. We'll produce a benchmark projection.
[05:47] Daniel: does Redwood provide a deployment orchestration, or do we need to run k8s?
[05:52] Priya: we provide an orchestration control plane that can run on customer k8s or in an air-gapped appliance mode. For large enterprises we often ship a control-plane that you host behind your firewall; the runtime sits on your k8s.
[06:05] Maria: about support SLAs - we need 24x7 support during prod and a dedicated TAM for escalations. what's offered?
[06:12] Alex: enterprise tier includes 24x7 support, dedicated TAM options, and on-call for major incidents. We'll map that to your needs in the proposal.
[06:20] Samir: instrumentation - we need token-level cost metrics and per-route tracing. can that all stay internal?
[06:27] Priya: yes, it's local telemetry; we expose dashboards in Redwood Console that can be hosted internally or we can stream raw events to your observability backend.
[06:36] Daniel: any regulatory gotchas? e.g., data residency for international trials?
[06:41] Alex: Redwood supports region pinning and private deployments in specific data centers; for international residency we'll discuss region-specific deployments. For strictly on-prem air-gapped, residency is by definition local.
[06:53] Maria: penetration testing - do you allow red-team assessments and provide test plans?
[06:58] Priya: yes, we have a standard penetration testing agreement and will provide a test plan and expected attack surface. We also support code reviews on request under NDA.
[07:10] Samir: curious about model lifecycle - can we pin model versions and control rollouts?
[07:16] Jordan: absolutely. the control plane allows pinning, canary rollouts, automatic fallback to previous model, and A/B testing. audit trails include model diffs.
[07:27] Daniel: how do you handle failures when offline? e.g., model download fails mid-update - is there a safe rollback?
[07:34] Priya: the update agent validates the bundle before applying; partial failure triggers automatic rollback to the prior state. We also recommend staging in a sandbox environment first.
[07:46] Maria: what's the expected operator footprint? can our SREs handle day-to-day or do we need Redwood ops involvement?
[07:53] Jordan: day-to-day can be handled by your SREs; we provide runbooks and a managed support option if you want us to handle ops under an SKO.
[08:02] Samir: we run internal evals - can we bring our own eval harness and run regressions after updates?
[08:08] Priya: yes you can run your evals; we can also plug into Redwood Optimize to track quality regressions against baseline prompt sets.
[08:18] Daniel: budget questions - we need both CapEx and OpEx breakdowns, because some stakeholders prefer capital purchases for on-prem.
[08:25] Alex: we'll include both pricing scenarios in the proposal.

[08:40] (some crosstalk, background noise)

[09:05] Priya: quick clarifying question for Maria - when you say 7 year retention, is that for raw transcripts or only audit records?
[09:12] Maria: audit records and any metadata needed for compliance; raw transcripts can be redacted or stored shorter. we'll follow up with exact policy.

[09:25] Samir: one more thing - model quantization: do you support post-training quantization pipelines or do we need to supply quantized weights?
[09:33] Priya: we support running quantization tools as part of onboarding and can accept quantized weights. for some models we recommend specific kernel builds which we can help produce.

[09:45] Daniel: stakeholders - legal and procurement will need procurement/SLA docs, InfoSec will need security docs, and the ML team needs a deep-dive POC with benchmarks.
[09:56] Alex: understood, we'll bundle the docs and propose a POC scope.

[10:08] Priya: next technical steps: we suggest a follow-up 60-90 minute deep-dive focused on hardware sizing and offline update walkthroughs. suggested attendees: Samir, Renee, Maria, and our infra engineer.
[10:22] Maria: sounds good. Daniel: yes let's aim for the week of March 23rd.

[10:30] Alex: great - i'll recap actions.

Recap / Next steps:
- Alex to send pricing, private deployment checklist, and SOC2/ISO references by 2026-03-15.
- Priya to prepare GPU sizing spreadsheet and schedule deep-dive for week of 2026-03-23.
- Maria to share compliance retention policy and regulatory POC contact by 2026-03-20.
- Customer to confirm pilot scope and internal stakeholders for procurement by 2026-03-18.

(End of meeting)
